title: A fibre core meeting its cladding
caption: Core n = 1.48 against cladding n = 1.46 gives sin θ_c = 1.46/1.48, so θ_c = 80.6° from the normal. A ray meeting the boundary at 75° is below it and leaks into the cladding (bending to 78.3°); at 85° it is totally internally reflected. Only rays nearly parallel to the fibre axis are guided.
alt: Two ray diagrams at a core–cladding boundary: a ray at 75° escapes into the cladding at 78.3°; a ray at 85° is totally internally reflected; the critical angle is 80.6°.
description: The critical angle is sin⁻¹(1.46/1.48) = 80.6° measured from the normal to the boundary.
A ray at 75° is less than 80.6°, so part of it refracts into the cladding, bending away from the normal to 78.3°.
A ray at 85° exceeds the critical angle: all the light is reflected back into the core.
Because the critical angle is so close to 90°, only rays travelling at less than about 9° to the axis are trapped.
